profile.reading: K-Motion Interactive is a sports-technology company that makes 3D motion-capture and biomechanics analysis systems used in golf and baseball swing instruction, based in the Scottsdale area of Maricopa County, Arizona. The coordinates on file sit within the McDowell Mountain Business Park, a multi-tenant office and light-industrial park, and a check of the address today finds a different small business occupying that specific building. There is no indication that K-Motion, or any current tenant at this location, operates server rooms, colocation space, or dedicated data center infrastructure here. This entry describes the business as it is known publicly rather than presenting an ordinary office address as a data center facility.

reading.body:
K-Motion Interactive is not a data center, and its presence in a data center inventory is a tagging error, not a facility.

The entry came from an OpenStreetMap point tagged as a data center. The coordinates resolve to a multi-tenant office and light-industrial building in McDowell Mountain Business Park in Scottsdale, Arizona, where a different small business now operates. K-Motion itself is a sports biomechanics and motion-capture company selling 3D swing analysis for golf and baseball. No server rooms, colocation space, or dedicated compute infrastructure are present.

The error matters because it is not isolated. The research note records that this address sits 12 to 15 miles from the other eight rows in the same batch, so those nine facilities are not one shared building. Each is an independently mistagged small business scattered across the Phoenix metro. Arizona has 56 mapped facilities, and only 4 of them publish power figures, totaling 512 MW. This entry adds nothing to that total.

What the data does not show is how many other entries in the wider inventory rest on the same kind of bad source. It also cannot say whether the 512 MW figure is complete or merely the portion that happens to be published. A count of mapped facilities is not a count of capacity, and a mistag is indistinguishable from a real facility until someone checks the address.
